pr.body:
Default timetable text can wash out over a bright sky, and elapsed rows fade names and times through parent opacity. This gives ordinary cells a local dark backing and keeps information fully opaque, while subduing elapsed rows through tint and border treatment. NEXT keeps its approved opaque accent and dark text; CURRENT keeps its separate inset. Optional contrast remains optional.

The authored change is confined to the timetable CSS in `src/native/index.html`, with canonical root/offline regeneration, focused fixture/contrast tests and DESIGN documentation. Typography, cell/card geometry, header/footer, frozen V1, builder/embed interfaces and scientific/motion owners are preserved.

Validation and evidence:

- 38 source-bound native Chromium/Firefox cases pass across the required scenes, viewports, DPRs, date states and white stress. Lowest measured intended foreground/background contrast: **4.859:1**, against the unchanged **4.5:1** requirement.
- Six native mutants reach the intended opacity/contrast failure; 78 focused source controls pass. Fresh RED, original failures, two native text/background pairs and all twelve text rectangles are retained.
- Canonical rebuild reproduces the qualified runtime; only root/offline change among 135 runtime files. Frozen V1 payload and current public V1 hashes match.
- Geometry: 29 exact cross-load comparisons; nine Firefox current-prayer-label Y offsets remain recorded. Exact old/new rule reversal in the same settled native page causes no movement. The precise original boot-time cause remains unestablished; no tolerance is widened.
- The pre-existing optional V1 Pages preflight rejects the existing Jekyll config at both base and candidate. That failure remains retained; payload verification and actual public V1 readback pass.
